key_insight: Mapping each bit-plane to its own mat group would let a low-precision read activate only those mats, cutting activation energy, not just bus bits.
killer_doubt: Activation senses the whole row; skipping planes needs FGDRAM-style partial wordlines and a JEDEC die change. Static 4-bit weights leave dynamic precision maybe <20% of traffic (estimate).
decisive_experiment: Ramulator2 plus DRAMPower model of plane-to-mat mapping with partial activation, driven by LLM decode traces carrying per-access precision; kill if total DRAM energy falls less than 25%. About $30k.
prior_art: Fine-Grained DRAM (NVIDIA, MICRO 2017); Half-DRAM (ISCA 2014); Any-Precision LLM bit-plane weights; R22 I-05653 precision-select column command (DROP).

key_insight: Interval bounds from fetched MSB planes make termination exact: skipped planes cost no accuracy or retraining. Best fit is K-cache scoring for top-k attention, where ordering, not values, matters.
killer_doubt: LeOPArd (ISCA 2022) already terminates bit-serially and exactly, ~1.8x energy, on chip. In DRAM each extra plane round trip adds ~100 ns, and only comparison-fed operations qualify.
decisive_experiment: Dump INT8 K caches from an open 70B model on LongBench at 32k context; compute exact per-plane bounds for top-2% selection; measure K bytes skipped. Kill below 40%. About $20k GPU time.
prior_art: LeOPArd (ISCA 2022) exact bit-serial early termination (via search snippet); SpAtten progressive MSB fetch (HPCA 2021); SnaPEA; in-study I-02063 (HOLD).

key_insight: One plane-major copy serves several precisions. Its value is as the storage layout under I-02172's exact early termination or MSB-plane KV scoring, not as a standalone gain.
killer_doubt: Published any-precision layouts already do this. Batched decode fetches the most planes any token needs, so realistic saving is ~1.1-1.3x of decode traffic, not 2-4x.
decisive_experiment: Not needed for novelty. If pursued: an FPGA HBM controller replaying batched-decode traces with plane-major layout, measuring bytes moved against a native INT4 baseline. About $50k.
prior_art: Any-Precision LLM (ICML 2024); Matryoshka Quantization (2025); Stripes bit-serial accelerator; in-study I-02632 and I-09970 (DROP).

key_insight: An FPGA controller with a plane-major layout is the right cheap demo vehicle for the bit-plane family; same core mechanism as I-01714.
killer_doubt: The top 4 planes of FP16 are the sign plus 4 exponent bits, with zero mantissa, so the pass is unusable without nested integer quantization, which is published.
decisive_experiment: Software first (~$5k): perplexity of an 8B model reading the top N planes of FP16 versus INT8 plane-major weights, before any FPGA work.
prior_art: Any-Precision LLM (ICML 2024) bit-plane weights; Matryoshka Quantization (2025); in-study I-01714 (duplicate), I-02632 and I-11576 (DROP).

key_insight: Trading DRAM for compute suits a memory shortage: hashed IDs into a small MLP, plus exact rows for the hottest ~1%, could cut recommender tables 10-100x.
killer_doubt: Published DHE and MP-Rec. Each lookup becomes ~1-10 MFLOP instead of a ~256 B read (10-100x more compute); ~0.1% AUC loss matters, so production keeps int4 hashed tables.
decisive_experiment: Train hybrid DHE against int4 hashed tables on Criteo-1TB at equal AUC; report GB saved per added GFLOP and serving cost at current DRAM and GPU prices. About $40k of compute.
prior_art: Deep Hash Embedding (KDD 2021); MP-Rec hybrid (2023); TT-Rec (MLSys 2021); Google Unified Embedding; R30 I-06735 (DROP).

key_insight: With every row and column actively driven, crossbar currents sum linearly, so the read becomes matrix inversion in an interface chiplet rather than a selector problem.
killer_doubt: IR drop breaks linearity: a 1k-cell 20 nm line is ~2.5 kOhm; ~0.5 mA summed current drops ~0.6 V, above a 0.2 V read bias (estimate). ReRAM endures only ~1e6-1e10.
decisive_experiment: Build a 128x128 selector-less HfOx crossbar at a university fab; read it with Hadamard patterns and a least-squares decoder; measure bit error rate against array size and line resistance. About $250k.
prior_art: Imperial/Southampton mCAT multi-port readout with mathematical sneak-current cancellation (via search snippet); one-step row readout (arXiv 1903.01512); Cassuto sneak-path coding [training knowledge].

key_insight: It diagnoses MXT's failure correctly: compress only far-tier lines behind CXL, where ~150-250 ns already hides decompression, so ~1.5-2x ratios become capacity.
killer_doubt: Already productized: Marvell Structera A ships inline LZ4 and ZeroPoint licenses compression IP. Incompressible or encrypted pages (~1.0x) overflow a fixed advertised capacity, forcing OS ballooning.
decisive_experiment: Not needed for novelty. To size it: replay fleet memory dumps through LZ4 and BDI at 64 B to 4 KB granularity and measure capacity at p99 compressibility. About $20k.
prior_art: IBM MXT (2000-01); Marvell Structera A inline LZ4 (2024); ZeroPoint Technologies IP; R17 I-05749 and R28 I-09017 (DROP).

key_insight: Decentralized, lease-based page lending needs no central pool manager and recalls memory when a donor's pressure rises: wafer-free capacity at 4x prices.
killer_doubt: Microsoft Pond measured ~7% DRAM savings at 16-socket pools, not 10-15% of supply. On one CXL switch every peer is one hop, so gradient diffusion reduces to a central allocator.
decisive_experiment: Replay Azure and Alibaba memory traces through a 32-node simulator comparing gradient diffusion with a central Pond-style allocator; kill if it recovers under 3 points more GB at the p99 SLO. About $30k.
prior_art: Microsoft Pond (ASPLOS 2023); Memtrade (SIGMETRICS 2023); Infiniswap (NSDI 2017); diffusion load balancing (Cybenko 1989); CXL pooling appliances.

key_insight: Retired DDR4 is wafer-free capacity. An FPGA CXL card with pattern screening turns it into a cold tier at ~10-20% of new cost per bit during a 4x spike.
killer_doubt: Already shipping: Marvell Structera X and Meta Vistara reuse whole DDR4 DIMMs over CXL. Open-market feedstock may be ~1-2 EB/yr against ~30+ EB/yr of new bits (estimate).
decisive_experiment: Buy 200 retired RDIMMs (~$10k) and test retention, hammer and timing margins on an FPGA rig; publish yield and tail. About $60k, but it settles only the feedstock question.
prior_art: Marvell Structera X; Meta Vistara; Microsoft GreenSKU (ISCA 2024); R16 I-00224 (canonical HOLD); ITAD resellers.

key_insight: Chip-level harvest frees dies from the DIMM form factor, and hammer screening plus weak-row map-out is the right trust layer for aged DDR4.
killer_doubt: Desoldering adds a ~260 C reflow and ~1-3% package fallout for no gain, since DDR4 CXL controllers already accept whole DIMMs. Duplicate of I-00348 and I-00224.
decisive_experiment: As for I-00348, plus a 100-package reball pilot measuring reflow fallout and retention shift; kill chip-level harvest if fallout exceeds 1%. About $40k.
prior_art: Marvell Structera X; Meta Vistara (physics R14, via search snippet); Microsoft GreenSKU; R14 I-04852 desolder harvest (DROP).

key_insight: Aging-aware refresh and per-rank ECC remap inside the CXL controller let graded DDR4 bins serve as tier-2 memory without host changes.
killer_doubt: Duplicate of I-00348. Shipping CXL controllers already do ECC and post-package repair; the DDR4 pool is one-time and shrinks as fleets move to DDR5.
decisive_experiment: As for I-00348, plus measure how much capacity aging-aware refresh rescues beyond pass/fail retest; kill if under 5%. About $60k.
prior_art: Marvell Structera X; Meta Vistara; Microsoft GreenSKU (ISCA 2024); REAPER retention profiling; R16 I-06172 (DROP).
